Heavily infected cattle, sheep, goats and camels grow slowly, lose condition, produce less milk and meat, and become more open to other diseases. Young animals are often the most affected. Regular, well-planned deworming protects growth and productivity and can save the cost of treating sick animals later. HOW TO USE IT Albafas is given by mouth as a drench. The dose depends on the animal species and body weight, so follow the dose on the label and use an accurate drenching gun. Weigh or estimate weight carefully, and dose the heaviest animal in a group at its own weight to avoid under-dosing. Under-dosing is one of the main causes of worms becoming resistant to dewormers. If you are not sure about the dose, the correct time to treat, or the withdrawal period for milk and meat, ask your vet or animal health provider. GOOD PRACTICE • Deworm on a programme agreed with your vet, rather than only when animals look sick • Keep clean water and good pasture management to reduce re-infection • Rotate dewormers from different groups when advised, to help slow resistance • Keep records of dates, products and doses SAFETY AND STORAGE For veterinary use. Follow the label dose and withdrawal periods. Wear gloves when handling and wash your hands afterwards. Keep out of reach of children. Store the bottle tightly closed in a cool, dry place away from direct sun and food. Do not let rinse water reach streams or ponds. item.description: E-POS 80MM THERMAL RECEIPT PRINTER IN KENYA The E-POS 80mm Thermal Receipt Printer is a point-of-sale printing device for businesses that need to produce clear transaction receipts at a checkout or service counter. It is intended for use with a compatible POS system and suitable 80mm thermal paper. Thermal receipt printing uses heat-sensitive paper, so the printer can produce text without a conventional ink cartridge or toner. This makes it a practical option for shops and service businesses that print customer receipts throughout the working day. A PRACTICAL PRINTER FOR BUSY COUNTERS A receipt printer is an important part of a point-of-sale workflow. After a sale is recorded in compatible POS software, the system can send the transaction details to the printer so the customer receives a printed record. Depending on the software and configuration, receipts may show items purchased, quantities, prices, totals, taxes, payment details and the business information configured in the POS system. The exact receipt layout is controlled by the software, not by the printer alone. The 80mm paper format provides a wider receipt area than smaller receipt formats. This can be useful where a business needs room for longer item descriptions, several line items or additional transaction information. Confirm the supported paper width and roll dimensions against the actual unit and the paper you intend to buy before ordering. HOW THERMAL RECEIPT PRINTING WORKS Direct thermal printers create an image by applying heat to specially coated thermal paper. Because the printing process does not use ink cartridges, businesses do not need to purchase ink or toner for ordinary receipt printing. The paper itself is the consumable. Store thermal rolls in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, excess heat and friction, which can affect print quality or cause receipts to darken. For consistent results, load the roll in the direction indicated by the printer's paper guide, keep the paper path clear and use rolls that meet the printer's stated width and diameter limits. If a receipt prints blank, check that the thermal paper is loaded with its coated side facing the print head. Follow the manufacturer's instructions when opening the cover or clearing a paper jam. WHERE IT CAN BE USED An 80mm thermal receipt printer may suit retail shops, supermarkets, mini-markets, pharmacies, restaurants, cafés, salons, repair counters, ticket desks and other businesses that use compatible point-of-sale software. It can support routine checkout operations by giving customers a printed record and helping staff maintain a consistent transaction process. The printer is a peripheral device; it does not independently manage stock, calculate sales or process card and mobile-money payments. Those functions depend on the connected POS software and payment equipment. CHECK COMPATIBILITY BEFORE PURCHASE Before buying, confirm the connection type supported by the exact E-POS model, such as USB, Ethernet, serial or wireless connectivity. Do not assume that every connection option is included. Check operating-system support, driver availability and compatibility with your POS application. If the printer is intended for a cash drawer, confirm that the unit has the required cash-drawer port and that the drawer and software use a compatible interface. Also verify the power adapter, plug type, paper-roll dimensions and any cables or accessories included in the package. SETUP AND EVERYDAY CARE Install the correct driver or select the printer through the POS software according to the supplier's instructions. Print a test receipt before using the device for live transactions. Keep the printer on a stable, dry counter with enough space for the paper cover to open. item.title: Rafiki Rat and Mouse Glue Board
item.description: RAFIKI RAT AND MOUSE GLUE BOARD IN KENYA The Rafiki Rat and Mouse Glue Board is a foldable adhesive board intended for rodent monitoring and capture in selected indoor situations. It provides a non-bait alternative to rodenticide and can help identify activity in stores, offices and other suitable premises. Glue boards are not appropriate for every site or every situation, and their use must take account of animal-welfare requirements, children, pets and non-target wildlife. Check local guidance and the product instructions before deciding whether an adhesive board is suitable. HOW AN ADHESIVE BOARD WORKS The board uses a sticky surface to hold a rodent that contacts it. Its foldable design can help form a shallow tray or protected placement shape, depending on the product instructions. A glue board does not attract rodents from long distances and should not be expected to solve an infestation by itself. Placement needs to be based on signs of activity and an understanding of rodent movement. Use the board only in a way that complies with the supplier's directions and applicable rules. ASSESS THE SITE FIRST Look for droppings, gnaw marks, rub marks, tracks, damaged food packaging and other evidence before placing monitoring equipment. Identify likely routes along walls and behind equipment, while considering whether the location can be checked frequently. Do not put a glue board where children, pets, birds or other non-target animals can reach it. Avoid damp, dusty or high-traffic areas where the adhesive may become ineffective or the board may be disturbed. Do not place it near food, utensils or food-contact surfaces. INSPECTION IS ESSENTIAL A glue board must be checked frequently and should never be left unattended for extended periods. Establish an inspection schedule appropriate to the site and product instructions. If an animal is captured, follow the applicable animal-welfare and local handling requirements; do not improvise or leave it to suffer. If the board becomes dusty, wet, damaged or contaminated, replace it and dispose of it responsibly. Wear suitable protective equipment when handling used boards and wash hands after service. WHEN TO CONSIDER AN ALTERNATIVE For sites with children, pets, wildlife or high non-target exposure risk, a secured mechanical trap or a professionally managed rodent programme may be more appropriate. In some situations, tamper-resistant bait stations or live-capture equipment may be selected after a risk assessment. No single device is suitable for every building. A pest-management professional can help compare options based on the rodent species, activity level, hygiene requirements and site users. REDUCE FOOD AND SHELTER Rodent control should include practical prevention. Store food, animal feed and ingredients in sealed, rodent-resistant containers. Keep refuse bins closed and clean spills promptly. Remove clutter and nesting material, repair leaks and close suitable gaps around doors, pipes and wall penetrations. Check delivery areas and storerooms regularly, because new stock and packaging can conceal signs of rodent activity. Continue monitoring after the immediate problem appears to have reduced. PRODUCT DETAILS TO CONFIRM This listing is for one Rafiki Rat and Mouse Glue Board. Confirm the board dimensions, fold configuration, adhesive type and any stated service or disposal instructions from the current pack. Do not assume that the board is suitable for outdoor use or for every rodent size. Keep unused boards in their packaging and store them away from heat, dust, children and pets. BUY RAFIKI RAT AND MOUSE GLUE BOARDS IN KENYA Order the Rafiki Rat and Mouse Glue Board from Stermont Arcade for suitable indoor monitoring needs. item.title: Combat Tamper-Resistant Rodent Bait Station
item.description: COMBAT TAMPER-RESISTANT RODENT BAIT STATION IN KENYA The Combat Tamper-Resistant Rodent Bait Station is an enclosed placement device used as part of a planned rat and mouse management programme. A bait station provides a defined location for compatible rodent bait and helps keep bait contained instead of leaving it exposed on floors, shelves or open ground. It is intended for controlled placement and monitoring in appropriate residential, commercial and industrial settings. The station is not rodent bait itself, and purchasing the housing does not by itself eliminate rodents. WHY USE AN ENCLOSED BAIT STATION Loose bait can be disturbed, contaminated or reached by people and non-target animals. A suitable tamper-resistant station helps restrict casual access when it is correctly locked, secured and positioned. It can also protect bait from some dust, debris and environmental exposure. For pest-management professionals, fixed bait points make it easier to map activity, inspect consumption and maintain a consistent service record. The station should always be treated as one part of a broader integrated programme that includes sanitation, proofing and monitoring. SUITABLE LOCATIONS AND PLANNING Potential locations may include building perimeters, service corridors, utility areas, waste-management zones and other places where rodent signs have been identified. The exact placement depends on the site, rodent behaviour, station design and the label directions for the bait selected. A trained operator should assess likely runways, entry points, harbourage and food sources before installing stations. Do not place bait stations in food-preparation areas or where bait could contaminate food, utensils or packaging. Avoid positions where routine cleaning, deliveries or vehicle movement could damage or dislodge the unit. USING THE STATION RESPONSIBLY Use only bait or compatible monitoring inserts that are suitable for this specific station. Confirm the station's internal dimensions and bait-retention method before ordering replacement bait. Follow the rodenticide label for approved use, handling, inspection and disposal. Do not cut, break or repackage bait unless the product instructions expressly permit it. Keep bait and the station secured away from children, pets, livestock and wildlife. Where a site requires a documented pest-control programme, label and map each station in line with the operator's procedures and applicable requirements. INSPECTION AND SERVICE RECORDS A station should not be installed and then forgotten. Check it at intervals appropriate to the site risk and product label. During inspection, confirm that the housing remains closed and secured, the station has not moved, and the bait or monitoring insert has not been damaged or contaminated. Record the station reference, location, inspection date, observations and any service action. If there is evidence of tampering, damage, non-target access or bait spillage, secure the area and follow the product safety instructions. Never handle rodenticide bait with bare hands. INTEGRATED RODENT MANAGEMENT Bait stations work best alongside practical measures that reduce the conditions attracting rodents. Keep refuse in closed containers, remove food spills, store food and animal feed in rodent-resistant containers, and correct leaking water sources. Seal suitable gaps around pipes, doors and service penetrations with materials appropriate to the structure. Manage vegetation and clutter around buildings where these create hiding places. Monitor droppings, gnaw marks, tracks and other signs to understand whether activity is changing. If activity continues, reassess the site rather than relying on bait alone. The cable must move smoothly and allow the throttle to return to its closed position when released. This machine is intended for trained pest-management, vector-control or sanitation operators and should be selected according to the treatment plan, target pest, site conditions and the formulation label. Thermal foggers use heat; ULV cold foggers use mechanical atomisation. These methods are not interchangeable. Use only chemicals whose labels specifically permit the intended application method, dilution and droplet range. Fogging does not replace inspection, sanitation, source reduction, exclusion or a complete integrated pest-management programme. Before ordering, confirm the exact model and revision, solution and fuel tank capacities, power or ignition arrangement, voltage and plug where applicable, nozzle configuration, accessories, current manufacturer manual, warranty, spare-parts availability and service support. Inspect tanks, caps, seals, hoses, valves, cables, fuel connections, nozzles, guards and mounting hardware before use. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for preparation, startup, shutdown, cleaning and storage. Never refill or service a hot thermal machine. Keep fuel away from ignition sources and hot surfaces. Keep electrical components dry. Wear the PPE specified by the chemical label, restrict access to the treatment area and follow ventilation and re-entry requirements. Confirm final landed price, availability, warranty and delivery arrangements for Kenya before payment. The operator must match this equipment to the treatment plan, target pest, site conditions and formulation label; tank volume and visible aerosol alone do not establish a safe application rate or treatment result. item.title: Women's All-Black Knit Slip-On Walking Sneakers
item.description: All-black knit slip-on sneakers with flexible mesh-style upper, easy-entry collar and matching dark sole. The monochrome finish works with leggings, travel outfits and everyday basics. Intended for general walking and casual wear. Confirm insole details and size before ordering because slip-on fits can differ from lace-up shoes. Clean with a damp cloth and air-dry. This pair should be selected according to fit, intended use and construction rather than appearance alone. The listed style and colour help identify the design, but the actual product label is needed to confirm upper materials, lining, outsole compound and model code. A casual sneaker, court-inspired shoe, platform design and running shoe can look similar while serving different purposes. Measure both feet while standing and compare the longer foot with the size chart for the exact brand and model. Check toe room, forefoot width, heel hold and the position of the arch. Numerical sizes are not fully consistent between brands or between men’s and women’s lasts. If the wearer is between sizes, request fit guidance before ordering rather than assuming the shoe will stretch. Inspect the construction details that affect daily comfort: tongue padding, collar shape, lace eyelets, stitching, toe reinforcement and the way the upper joins the sole. Knit or mesh appearance does not prove a particular fibre or breathability rating. Suede-style panels may be natural or synthetic. Confirm the actual materials from the product label before selecting a cleaning method. Match the outsole to the surface and activity. A flat court-style sole, a chunky fashion platform and a cushioned running-style midsole are not designed for identical movement. Look at tread depth, flex points, heel shape and outsole wear. Do not assume that the pair is waterproof, slip-resistant, orthopaedic or certified for work protection unless the exact model documentation confirms the feature. For everyday Kenyan use, consider commuting, school, errands, travel, casual office outfits and the surfaces on which the shoes will be worn. Wet pavements, dusty paths and long periods of standing can place different demands on footwear. A lifestyle sneaker may suit ordinary daily wear but should not replace certified protective shoes in workshops, construction sites or industrial workplaces. Clean the pair according to the confirmed material. Remove loose dirt with a soft brush or cloth, test any cleaner on a small hidden area and avoid soaking glued components. Knit and mesh panels need gentle cleaning; suede or suede-style surfaces may require a suitable brush. Allow shoes to air-dry naturally away from direct heat, which can affect adhesives and synthetic materials. Inspect the outsole, heel counter, stitching, eyelets and upper periodically for separation, worn tread or structural damage. Stop using the pair for demanding activity if damage affects fit or stability. Store footwear in a dry, ventilated place and allow it to dry after exposure to rain. Rotating pairs between uses can help the lining air out and reduce trapped moisture. Before payment, confirm the exact size, colour, pair condition, packaging and delivery arrangement. Ask for the actual box or tongue label when brand authenticity or model code matters. Product photography is useful for identifying style but can vary with lighting and screen settings. The current catalogue price is retained; reconfirm price and stock before checkout. A buyer should also inspect the insole, lining and interior finish. Check that seams do not create pressure points, the insole sits flat and the heel lining is not damaged. If removable insoles are important, confirm that feature with the seller. Try the pair on both feet with the socks normally worn, then walk on a clean surface to assess comfort before removing tags. The product name and colour description are useful for online search, but the actual pair remains the final reference for colour, material and finish.…

item.title: Advance In-Ground Termite Monitoring Station
item.description: The Advance in-ground station is a perimeter monitoring unit used in structured subterranean termite inspection programmes. Its durable housing is installed in soil at planned monitoring points, allowing trained technicians to inspect the station and check for termite activity without opening the building fabric. The station supports monitoring and follow-up decisions; it is not, by itself, a complete termite treatment or a guarantee against infestation. Position and inspect it according to the system instructions and local site conditions. This listing is for the monitoring station hardware; cartridges or bait components may be separate and should be confirmed before ordering. An in-ground monitoring station is an access point in a planned perimeter inspection system. It allows a technician to check for termite activity at selected locations and document changes over time. The station housing does not itself create a chemical barrier, kill a colony or guarantee that a building is termite-free. Its value depends on correct placement and routine inspection. Begin with a site survey of foundations, expansion joints, service penetrations, damp areas, landscaping, timber in contact with soil and locations with previous termite evidence. A trained technician should plan station positions so that each can be located and inspected. Avoid locations likely to be flooded, paved over, disturbed by construction or damaged by vehicle traffic. Confirm exactly what the package includes. Station housing, inspection inserts, monitoring devices and active bait cartridges may be separate components depending on the system and supplier package. Do not describe the hardware as containing an active ingredient unless the supplied label confirms it. Check compatibility with the exact Advance system and obtain the current installation instructions. Prepare a station map and assign each installed point a unique identifier. Record the installation date, location, surrounding conditions and any relevant building observations. During each inspection, note the station condition, moisture, disturbance and evidence of termite activity. Consistent records help compare visits and identify changes that would be missed by an unrecorded visual check. Monitoring intervals should follow the manufacturer instructions and the site risk profile. Keep covers accessible and replace damaged components only with compatible parts. A station that has been moved, flooded, blocked or buried under landscaping may no longer provide useful information. Do not assume that an unattended station provides continuous protection or that absence of activity at one point proves the whole property is clear. If activity is detected, a qualified pest-management professional should identify the termite and assess the building before selecting a response. Depending on the situation, an integrated plan may involve bait components, targeted treatment, moisture correction, removal of conducive conditions, physical repairs and follow-up inspections. Monitoring hardware alone is not a complete termite treatment. For homes, hotels, warehouses, schools and commercial properties, explain to the client what the station does and does not do. It can support early detection and evidence-based decisions, but it cannot guarantee that termites will not enter a structure. Document inspections, treatment products, active ingredients, follow-up work and any warranty terms accurately. A perimeter station is most useful when the monitoring programme has a clear baseline. At installation, record the building condition, visible conducive factors and known termite history. Mark stations on a plan that can be used by different technicians and retain photographs of the initial placement. This makes later inspections more consistent and helps explain any changes to the property owner. Do not place stations where routine mowing, excavation, drainage work or landscaping will repeatedly disturb them. Tell the property…

item.title: Catchmaster 909 Replacement Fly Light Glue Boards – 12 Pack
item.description: Catchmaster 909 replacement adhesive boards are consumables for compatible insect light traps. The sticky insert captures flying insects attracted to the unit’s UV lamp and provides a visible record that can support routine monitoring in commercial premises. Replace boards when loaded, dusty or outside the service interval recommended by the trap manufacturer. Before ordering, compare the board dimensions and mounting pattern with the model installed at your site; compatibility varies between light-trap brands. This listing is for replacement glue boards, not a complete UV light unit. The 909 is a Catchmaster manufacturer part number. Published supplier specifications give a full-size board measuring approximately 16. 375 by 9. 06 inches and describe a perforated centre line that can divide the insert into two narrower pieces for certain compatible units. Supplier compatibility lists name several Vector, Mantis, Gardner and Gilbert models. This does not mean that the insert fits every insect light trap. Compare the installed unit's board channel, retaining points, colour requirement and dimensions before ordering. If the existing insert has a different outline or mounting tabs, verify the replacement rather than forcing it into the housing. An adhesive insert provides a visible record of insects captured at the trap location. During a service visit, a technician can note the catch type, approximate quantity, date and room. Comparing observations over several visits can help identify recurring pressure near receiving doors, waste areas, loading bays or other access points. A rising catch count should trigger investigation of sanitation, door discipline, screens, lighting and possible breeding sources. The board is evidence for a monitoring record; it is not a complete insect-control programme and does not show the full insect population in a building. Before installation, isolate or switch off the light trap in accordance with its own instructions. Remove the used insert without brushing captured insects onto nearby surfaces. Keep fingers away from the adhesive face and place the replacement in the manufacturer's guides so that it lies flat. Do not cover the UV lamp, obstruct ventilation or modify the trap to accommodate an incorrectly sized board. Record the date and trap location after fitting. If the board is perforated, split it only where the trap design calls for a narrower insert. Glue-board light traps are used in suitable indoor locations in hotels, restaurants, supermarkets, food processing rooms, warehouses, hospitals and retail facilities. Position the trap to monitor flying insects without drawing them across exposed food or clean work surfaces. Avoid direct sunlight, strong competing light and locations where air movement prevents insects from reaching the unit. A site survey should consider doors, windows, waste handling, receiving points and the direction of insect movement before the trap is mounted. In food premises, coordinate placement with the site's hygiene and food-safety procedures. Check the board at the frequency specified by the trap maker and the site's pest-management schedule. Replace it when adhesive is covered, dusty, contaminated, damaged or no longer suitable for capturing insects. High dust levels, grease, moisture and heat can shorten useful service life. Keep a service log with the board change date, trap identifier, catch observations and corrective action. If a board fills quickly, investigate the cause rather than simply changing inserts more often. Consistent records help managers assess whether proofing or housekeeping improvements are working. Keep unused boards in their original packaging until needed. Store them flat in a cool, dry place away from dust, direct sunlight and excessive heat so the adhesive is protected. Avoid bending the board or placing heavy objects on the pack. During servicing, use gloves if required by the facility hygiene procedure, avoid contact with captured…

item.title: SA-1600 Lockable Automatic Insecticide Aerosol Dispenser
item.description: The SA-1600 is a wall-mountable automatic dispenser designed for compatible 300 ml metered aerosol cans. Its lockable housing helps protect the refill and supports scheduled release intervals in suitable commercial spaces such as service corridors, washrooms and approved non-food handling areas. The dispenser is a delivery accessory and does not replace an integrated pest-management plan, sanitation or exclusion work. Confirm the refill valve compatibility and programming options before use. Install it where the aerosol label permits, away from food, direct contact and children, and follow the refill manufacturer’s room-size and ventilation directions. The SA-1600 is a timed dispenser housing for a compatible metered aerosol refill. The device controls the release schedule; the can contains the active formulation and determines what the aerosol is intended to do. The dispenser does not identify insects, measure infestation levels or remove breeding sources. It should be selected only after the site has defined the target problem and checked that a metered aerosol application is allowed in the intended room under the refill's own label. The product listing refers to 300ml metered aerosol cans, but can volume alone does not guarantee fit. Valve stem, actuator design, can height and housing clearance can vary. Before purchase, compare the refill manufacturer's compatibility information with the SA-1600 unit. Do not force a can into the housing or modify the actuator. Confirm whether the unit is supplied with a key, batteries, mounting screws and an instruction sheet, because these items can differ between seller packages. Select a secure wall location where the aerosol outlet is not directed toward people, food, utensils, animal feed, medical supplies or a ventilation intake. Consider room occupancy, airflow, windows, fans and the normal movement of staff and visitors. A washroom or service corridor may be suitable only when the aerosol label permits it. Food premises should coordinate placement with their food-safety controls and avoid exposing open products or food-contact surfaces to the discharge. Read the dispenser manual and aerosol label before loading the can. Fit the refill according to the instructions, check that the actuator seats correctly and set only a schedule permitted for that product and room. More frequent discharge is not automatically more effective and may increase exposure or waste. Record the installation date, refill name, room, timer setting and responsible staff member. Test the device only as directed and keep people clear of the outlet during commissioning. Include the unit in a scheduled facilities inspection. Confirm that the housing remains secure and locked, the refill is correctly seated, the outlet is unobstructed and the battery or power supply is functioning. Replace the refill according to its label and the dispenser's service guidance. Record the date and product batch where relevant. If target pest activity continues, inspect doors, screens, waste, drains, standing water and other source conditions instead of simply increasing the aerosol release frequency. Use only a refill whose label authorises the intended pest, room type and metered dispensing method. Follow restrictions concerning people, children, pets, food, ventilation and re-entry. Keep aerosol cans away from heat and direct sunlight; do not puncture, burn or incinerate them. Staff responsible for servicing should understand the product's safety data and wear the PPE specified by the label. A locked housing helps control access but does not make an unsuitable aerosol safe for a room. In hotels, offices, retail buildings and other Kenyan facilities, automatic dispensers may form one small part of a documented hygiene programme. They should be combined with sanitation, waste control, fly screens, door management and inspection. Food businesses should check local regulatory and label requirements before using any pesticide product…

item.title: 3M 6700 Series Full-Face Respirator
item.description: The 3M 6700 Series full-face respirator is personal protective equipment intended for use with compatible, correctly selected filters or cartridges. The full-face design provides eye and respiratory coverage for trained workers when the complete respirator assembly is suitable for the chemical label, exposure assessment and workplace programme. Filter cartridges are not assumed to be included; verify size, cartridge type, approvals, condition and fit before purchase. A respirator must be fit-tested and maintained in line with the manufacturer’s instructions and applicable occupational safety requirements. It is not safe to use an unknown cartridge or to rely on a respirator where oxygen deficiency or an immediately dangerous atmosphere may exist. The 3M 6700 is the small-size facepiece in the 3M 6000 Series full-face respirator family. It is a reusable facepiece, not a universal filter and not automatically a complete respiratory-protection system. Compatible filters and cartridges must be selected for the identified hazard and used in an approved configuration. Confirm the genuine product marking, size and package contents before purchase. Cartridge selection requires a documented assessment of the contaminant, concentration, exposure duration, oxygen level and work conditions. Organic-vapour, particulate, acid-gas and combination cartridges are not interchangeable. Check the 3M compatibility matrix and the cartridge approval for the exact hazard. Never select a cartridge solely because it physically attaches to the facepiece. Fit testing is essential for each wearer and facepiece size. Facial hair across the sealing surface, eyewear interference, scars, incorrect strap adjustment or an unsuitable face shape can compromise the seal. A user seal check is required each time the respirator is donned, but it does not replace formal fit testing. A small-size facepiece may not fit every wearer. Air-purifying respirators must not be used in oxygen-deficient atmospheres, unknown concentrations or immediately dangerous conditions. Cartridge service life depends on contaminant, concentration, humidity, breathing rate and other factors. Follow a documented change schedule and never rely on smell alone as a warning. Consult the chemical safety data sheet and workplace respiratory-protection programme. Inspect the lens, inhalation and exhalation valves, harness, straps, face seal and cartridge connection points before every use. Remove damaged or distorted components from service. Clean and disinfect the facepiece only by the manufacturer-approved method, allow it to dry fully and store it away from dust, sunlight, heat, solvents and deformation. Filters and cartridges may be sold separately from the facepiece. Confirm exact compatible part numbers for the chemical and task, and check approval markings, shelf life, packaging integrity and replacement intervals. A general claim that a mask is suitable for fumigation is not sufficient to establish protection for a particular pesticide or exposure. For Kenyan pest-control employers, include the respirator in a written risk assessment and respiratory-protection programme. Match the PPE to the product label, safety data sheet and task; train workers; arrange fit testing; and define cartridge change schedules. Respiratory equipment does not make an unsafe application acceptable and must be combined with ventilation, exclusion and hygiene controls. A complete respiratory-protection programme should identify who is authorised to wear the equipment, which hazards require it, how fit testing is documented and when filters are replaced. Workers need practical training on donning, doffing, seal checks, cleaning, storage and emergency exit. Supervisors should review the programme when the chemical, process, exposure level or worker changes. A full-face respirator lens can become scratched, clouded or damaged, reducing visibility and potentially affecting safe work. Inspect it under good lighting and…

item.title: FNIRSI WMT-10 Pinless Wood Moisture Meter
item.description: The FNIRSI WMT-10 is a non-destructive moisture meter for checking moisture levels in timber and selected building materials during property inspections. Its pinless sensing approach helps technicians scan surfaces without leaving probe holes, while the display provides a quick reading for comparison across inspected areas. Moisture readings can help identify conditions that may contribute to timber deterioration and attract wood-damaging pests, but the meter does not detect termites directly and cannot confirm an infestation. Use it as one part of a wider inspection that includes visual checks, tapping and appropriate specialist tools. Verify material mode and calibration before recording readings. FNIRSI identifies the WMT-10 as an inductive, pinless instrument with a 2. 4-inch colour screen, 0. 1% display resolution and a maximum sensing depth of up to 17mm. The sensor area is listed as 40. 5 by 40. 5mm. Published ranges are 0–75% for hardwood and softwood, 0–25% for plaster wall and 0–43% for brick wall, with a stated measurement error of ±1. 5%. These are instrument specifications, not universal building moisture limits or a guarantee that every surface can be measured accurately. The instrument provides separate modes for hardwood, softwood, plaster wall and brick wall. Select the mode that best matches the surface being tested before taking a reading. A timber setting should not be used as though it were a calibrated plaster-wall setting. Different species, density, coatings and construction assemblies can influence readings. Compare like materials under similar conditions and consult the manufacturer's instructions when a surface is composite, painted, laminated or otherwise outside the listed measurement modes. Begin a building survey with a visual assessment of the timber, wall finish, plumbing routes, roof junctions, bathrooms, kitchens and other locations where moisture may accumulate. Use the meter to scan accessible areas and record the location, material mode and displayed value. Take several readings across the inspection area rather than relying on one point. Repeat measurements around an area of concern to understand whether the condition is localised or spread across a wider surface. Dated photographs and written notes help explain why a location was tested. The WMT-10 can help identify differences in moisture conditions in selected materials, but it does not locate a leak, identify the source of water or diagnose termite activity. A damp reading may relate to plumbing, roof leakage, condensation, ground moisture or another building issue. Termite confirmation requires other evidence, such as mud tubes, galleries, damaged timber or live insects. Use the meter as supporting information in a building or pest inspection, not as a stand-alone verdict or substitute for a qualified specialist. The 2. 4-inch colour display is intended to make readings easier to view during field work. FNIRSI lists sound and colour alarms, a temperature display, a built-in flashlight and the ability to save and review up to 30 sets of readings. The alarm thresholds should be understood in relation to the selected material mode. Stored readings can support a small inspection route, but larger jobs should also use a written report with room references, photographs and dated observations. Do not interpret an alarm as an automatic instruction to treat a building. Pinless meters sense a zone beneath the sensor rather than a single point at the surface. The maximum depth is specified as up to 17mm, but actual response can vary with material, contact, surface flatness and construction. Metal behind a wall, foil layers, dense coatings or uneven surfaces may affect the reading. Do not compare results from different modes as if they were directly equivalent. When a result has legal, structural or contractual importance, obtain confirmation using an appropriate reference method and follow the instrument manual. Keep the sensor area clean and…

item.title: B&G Versatool 415 Termite Treatment Injection Tool
item.description: The B&G Versatool 415 is a professional termite treatment delivery tool designed for trained operators who need to place compatible liquid termiticide at defined soil or structural locations. The tool is part of a termite treatment equipment system, not a ready-to-use pesticide. Its valve, pipe and selected tip control delivery to the treatment point. Correct selection and use depend on the building construction, product label, treatment plan and the exact kit configuration supplied. B&G's published information identifies the 415 as a Versatool termite tool kit with a valve featuring tip shut-off. A supplier specification for the 415 kit lists 12-inch and 40-inch 7/16-inch professional termite pipes, a 40-inch 5/8-inch professional rodding pipe, and several tips for soil rodding, void and directional delivery. The exact parts supplied with this listing must be verified before purchase; the model number alone should not be taken as proof that every accessory in a larger kit is included. The tip shut-off feature is intended to help the operator control flow at the delivery point and reduce unwanted discharge when repositioning the tool. B&G describes the Versatool system as compatible with selected pipe sizes and delivery tips for different treatment tasks. The operator must match the tip and pipe to the intended method and the pesticide label. Do not assume that a 7/16-inch void pipe and a 5/8-inch soil rodding pipe are interchangeable or that every tip fits every valve. Termite treatment begins with a proper inspection. Identify the evidence of termite activity, the building construction, slab edges, expansion joints, service penetrations, soil contact and previous treatment history. Determine whether the planned treatment method is permitted by the pesticide label and suitable for the site. Locate water, gas, electrical and communication services before drilling or inserting a pipe. A tool kit should be selected only after the operator knows which pipes, tips and access points the treatment plan requires. Before use, inspect the valve, pipe, tips, shut-off mechanism, seals and connectors. Confirm that all components are securely fitted and that the chosen tip is correct for the application. Follow B&G's instructions for pressure, flow, handling and maintenance. Do not force a pipe into an obstruction, apply pressure beyond the equipment rating or inject into an unknown void. The 415 kit is designed for professional application work; it should not be improvised as a general-purpose sprayer or used by an untrained person. The treatment product determines the permitted application rate, dilution, site, target pest, PPE and re-entry requirements. Use only pesticide products registered in Kenya for the intended purpose and follow the current label and safety data sheet. Wear the required protective clothing, gloves and eye protection, control access to the treatment area and prevent spills or runoff. Do not apply near drains, wells or water bodies unless the label explicitly permits the location and all environmental precautions are met. After treatment, clean or flush the equipment only as directed by the chemical label and B&G instructions. Manage rinsate and residues in accordance with the product label and local waste requirements; never discharge them into storm drains or surface water. Inspect the valve for leaks, check the tip for blockage and examine pipes for damage. Store the equipment securely, away from unauthorised users, and keep a maintenance record. Replace worn seals and damaged parts before the next job. For Kenyan pest-control businesses, the Versatool 415 may support professional termite work on suitable residential, commercial and institutional properties. Soil type, building design, slab thickness, drainage and buried services affect the treatment method. A technician should prepare a site-specific plan and explain the limits of the treatment to the property owner. The presence of a professional injection…

item.title: B&G Hand Dust-R 1152A Professional Duster
item.description: The B&G Hand Dust-R 1152A is a manual applicator for professional pest-control work where compatible insecticide dusts or granular formulations must be delivered to selected areas. Its reservoir, hand-operated pump and extension accessories are designed to help technicians distribute dry material in attics, crawl spaces and other suitable locations. This is application equipment, not a pesticide. The product label for the formulation being used determines the permitted target pest, site, method, rate and protective equipment. B&G's published specification states that the Hand Dust-R 1152A can hold up to 1. 5 pounds of insecticide dust or approximately 2 quarts of granules. The manufacturer lists a 3. 5-inch filling opening, a 12-inch extension with a 90-degree offset at the end and a selection of tips. B&G also describes an extension that adds static charge to the dust, helping material adhere to suitable surfaces. Confirm the exact tips and accessories supplied with this listing before purchase. The larger chamber makes the 1152A different from a compact bulb duster such as the B&G 1150. It is intended for jobs where a technician needs to carry a greater quantity of compatible dry formulation and apply it over a larger treatment route. The hand-operated mechanism does not require an electrical supply, which can be useful during service work in locations without convenient power. The reservoir capacity is a tool specification, not a recommendation to fill it completely or apply the entire contents at one site. Before filling the chamber, inspect the target area and review the pesticide label and safety data sheet. Confirm that the selected dust or granule is approved for the intended pest and application location. B&G identifies the tool for suitable applications in areas such as attics and crawl spaces, but the product label remains controlling. Do not assume that all formulations can be used in every void, roof space or outdoor location. Keep different formulations separate and label the equipment clearly to avoid cross-contamination. The large filling opening is intended to make loading easier, but material should be added carefully to avoid dust release. Use the correct tip and extension for the work area. B&G's product information describes a 12-inch offset extension and additional tip options for directing the discharge. The extension can help reach selected voids and overhead or awkward locations without placing the operator directly at the treatment point. Do not use the duster to create a cloud of material or apply more than the label allows. The manufacturer describes the pump as a way to propel dry formulations through the selected delivery arrangement. Follow the instructions for positioning the siphon tube and selecting a light or heavier application. The amount delivered can vary with formulation, tip, extension, pump movement and the orientation of the chamber. Test the operation only in a controlled, permitted area and follow the label's application method. If the tool blocks or dispenses unevenly, stop and clear it using the approved cleaning procedure rather than forcing the pump. For pest-control work, targeted dry formulation placement may be used in approved voids and harbourage sites as part of a wider programme. The technician should identify the target pest, inspect the building and decide whether dust or granules are appropriate. The tool does not replace sanitation, exclusion, moisture correction, monitoring or follow-up. In food premises, avoid contamination of exposed food, utensils and food-contact surfaces. Use only formulations and application methods authorised for the specific premises and comply with facility hygiene controls. Wear the personal protective equipment specified by the formulation label and control access to the treatment area. Avoid inhaling dust and prevent contact with skin and eyes. Do not use the duster near open food, people or animals unless the product label explicitly…

item.title: B&G Robco Soil Rodding Tool for Termite Treatment
item.description: The B&G Robco Soil Rodding Tool is a specialist applicator for trained termite technicians carrying out approved sub-slab and soil treatment procedures. Its extended steel shaft, footplate and delivery tip are designed to help place treatment through soil access points beneath or alongside concrete slabs. Correct use depends on the building construction, treatment label, soil conditions and a documented termite management plan. Confirm the shaft length, tip configuration and connection fittings before purchase. This is an application tool only; treatment chemicals are not included. Do not drill or inject into unknown services, and follow all safety and product-label requirements. B&G describes its Robco Soil Rodding Tool with a 40-inch pipe, a 5/8-inch 360-degree delivery tip and a footplate to assist rodding into soil. The manufacturer positions it as a sub-slab injector for applying termiticide beneath concrete, tile or wood flooring to reach voids for termite control. The exact assembly in this listing should be checked against the manufacturer's current product sheet. Do not assume that a valve, pump, hose, pressure regulator or additional tip is included unless the package details say so. Subterranean termites can enter structures from soil and may exploit joints, service penetrations and concealed spaces. A soil rodding tool is designed to help a trained operator place a labelled liquid treatment at selected locations in the soil or beneath a suitable slab. The 360-degree tip distributes material around the delivery point when used as specified. It is not a general-purpose garden lance, drain rod or tool for injecting arbitrary chemicals into walls and floors. A proper termite job begins with inspection of the building, construction type, slab edges, expansion joints, service penetrations, drainage and visible termite evidence. Identify electrical, water, gas and communication services before drilling or inserting a rod. Review the treatment product label and safety data sheet to confirm that sub-slab or soil application is permitted. Establish the intended treatment points and follow the labelled rate and procedure rather than improvising spacing, pressure or volume. Before use, inspect the pipe, footplate, tip, valve and connections for wear, blockage or leakage. Confirm that the selected components match the B&G tool and the treatment system. Use the footplate and rodding approach described in the equipment instructions, maintaining stable control of the shaft and delivery valve. Do not force the rod through an obstruction or exceed the equipment's rated pressure. Application quality depends on soil conditions, the treatment label and correct equipment setup. B&G offers several termite tools, pipes, valves and tips that may look similar but serve different applications. Verify the tool model, pipe diameter, thread or coupling, tip type and valve before ordering spares. A 5/8-inch rodding pipe should not be assumed to fit every 7/16-inch termite pipe or another manufacturer's valve. Confirm whether the supplied unit is a complete tool or an individual component. Ask the supplier to list the included parts in writing if the work plan requires a specific kit. Termiticide handling must follow the product label, Kenyan registration requirements and the site's risk assessment. Trained operators should wear the specified personal protective equipment, control access to the treatment area and prevent spills or runoff. Do not inject near unknown services, drains, wells or water bodies. Observe label requirements for mixing, ventilation, re-entry and waste disposal. A robust metal tool does not eliminate chemical exposure hazards or make an unapproved treatment method acceptable. After the job, clean or flush the delivery system only as directed by the equipment maker and the chemical label. Manage rinse water or chemical residue under the applicable waste procedure; do not discharge it into storm drains or surface water.…

item.title: Zippered Bed Bug Proof Mattress Encasement – Queen Size
item.description: A full-zip mattress encasement designed to create a protective physical barrier around a mattress during a bed bug prevention or management programme. The fitted cover encloses the mattress and helps reduce hiding places and simplify inspection of the sleeping surface. It is a monitoring and exclusion aid, not a stand-alone cure for an active infestation; bed frames, headboards, bedside furniture and surrounding rooms still require inspection and appropriate treatment. Check mattress dimensions and zipper closure before ordering. Keep the cover intact, inspect seams regularly and follow the care instructions so the barrier remains functional. Measure the mattress before selecting the queen size. Mattress dimensions are not identical across every manufacturer or market. Measure the width, length and depth, including any integrated pillow-top layer, before ordering. A cover that is too tight can put strain on the zipper and stitching; an oversized cover can bunch, shift or feel uncomfortable beneath bedding. Confirm the exact dimensions stated on the supplied product packaging rather than relying only on the word queen. If the mattress is unusually deep or has a topper, obtain a fit confirmation before purchase. Unlike a fitted sheet or thin mattress protector, a full encasement is intended to surround the mattress on all sides and close with a zipper. This creates a continuous outer surface that can make visual inspection easier and reduce the number of original mattress seams and folds available as hiding places. The zipper and its end closure are critical parts of the barrier. This listing does not claim a laboratory certification, a particular fabric rating or a guaranteed insect-proof performance beyond the physical cover design described. Remove bedding and inspect the mattress before fitting. Follow the maker's directions and, if the mattress is heavy, use two people to guide it into the cover without dragging it across sharp edges. Do not pull hard on the zipper or force fabric into its teeth. Check that corners are seated, the cover is not twisted and the closure reaches its intended end point. After installation, inspect the entire perimeter and confirm that no part of the mattress remains exposed. An encasement is a supportive barrier and inspection aid, not a treatment for the whole room. Bed bugs may remain in bed-frame joints, screw holes, headboards, bedside cabinets, upholstered furniture, skirting gaps, luggage and nearby rooms. A complete response includes a careful inspection, monitoring, appropriate treatment and follow-up checks. Where suitable, bed-leg interceptor cups can provide additional monitoring information. Do not tell customers that covering the mattress alone eradicates an infestation. Examine the fabric, seams, corners and zipper regularly for tears, punctures, loose stitching or a closure that no longer seals. Keep sharp tools, pets' claws and rough furniture edges away from the cover. Follow the actual care label for laundering and drying; high heat, bleach or aggressive cleaning can damage some materials. If the cover is torn or the zipper fails, treat the barrier as compromised and replace it or seek a repair method approved by the manufacturer. Record inspection dates in accommodation settings. In Kenyan homes, rental apartments, student hostels, guest houses and hotels, mattress encasements can support consistent housekeeping and bed bug monitoring. Multi-room accommodation should use a room-by-room inspection process instead of relying on covers only where bites are reported. Staff should know how to report sightings and suspicious marks promptly. When moving mattresses, protect them from contact with infested furniture and inspect bed frames and headboards as well. A standard procedure helps reduce the chance of carrying insects between rooms. Do not spray insecticide onto the cover or zipper unless the product label specifically permits that use. The encasement is a physical accessory,…

item.title: DuoTrap Bed Bug Interceptor Cups – 4 Pack
item.description: DuoTrap bed bug interceptor cups are passive monitoring devices designed to sit beneath suitable bed or furniture legs and help detect crawling insects moving between the floor and the furniture. The recessed cup arrangement is intended to create a difficult route out once an insect enters the inner well. Interceptors can help a homeowner, hotel team or pest technician monitor bed bug activity over time, but they are not a pesticide and do not treat an infestation by themselves. This listing is for a four-pack of interceptor cups. Interceptors are most useful when the furniture is configured so that every relevant leg rests securely inside a cup and the bed does not touch nearby walls, curtains or other furniture that could create an alternative route. Before installation, inspect the bed frame and surrounding area, move the bed into a suitable position and check that the floor is stable. If the bed has a central support, unusual leg shape or wheels, confirm that the cup can support it safely. Do not use an interceptor that rocks, cracks or cannot hold the furniture securely. The purpose of the cup is monitoring. Insects attempting to climb onto or leave the bed may encounter the interceptor surface, allowing the user to inspect for activity. Check the cups regularly and record the date, room and any insects found. A captured insect should be identified carefully; other crawling insects may also enter a monitor. If a bed bug is suspected, retain a sample or clear photograph for a qualified identification rather than relying only on an assumption based on bites or marks. Prepare the installation area by vacuuming and cleaning the floor around the bed legs. Place a cup beneath each suitable leg and ensure the furniture weight is supported in the centre of the cup as directed by the product design. Do not place the cup on a thick rug or uneven surface if that prevents stable contact. Keep bedding, bed skirts and electrical cables from touching the floor in a way that bypasses the monitor. If the bed is pushed against a wall, insects may use the wall as an alternative route and the monitoring result may be misleading. Inspect the cups on a planned schedule, such as during routine room checks or pest-management visits. Look for insects, dust, debris, cracks and any movement of the furniture that could dislodge the cups. Clean or replace the device according to its material and manufacturer guidance. Avoid applying oil, pesticide or powder to the interceptor unless the product instructions specifically permit it; altering the surface can affect the way insects move through the device and can compromise monitoring. Interceptors work best as part of a wider bed bug inspection. Check mattress seams, the bed base, headboard fixings, screw holes, bedside furniture, upholstered chairs, skirting and nearby cracks. Mattress encasements can simplify inspection of the mattress exterior, while laundering and appropriate treatment may be needed for affected items. Do not assume that an empty interceptor proves there are no bed bugs, because insects may be hiding elsewhere or using another route into the bed. For accommodation providers, record each interceptor's room and position so that catches can be compared over time. If a room changes occupancy, keep the monitor in place and check it during the room-turnover process. When a positive catch is found, follow the property's reporting and pest-management procedure. Avoid moving potentially infested furniture into another room without inspection. In multi-unit buildings, consider adjacent rooms and shared service routes when planning follow-up checks. The four-pack format is intended for a bed or other furniture arrangement with up to four suitable legs, but the actual number required depends on the furniture design. Confirm cup dimensions, opening size, weight-bearing suitability and compatibility with the leg shape before purchase. A bed with more than four support points may need additional…

item.title: 365nm UV Blacklight Inspection Flashlight
item.description: A 365nm UV blacklight inspection flashlight is a portable ultraviolet light source for supplementary visual checks during pest, hygiene and property inspections. Its narrow-beam illumination can make selected fluorescent residues, fibres and materials easier to see on suitable surfaces. This listing identifies a 365nm inspection flashlight, not a detector that identifies a pest species or proves an infestation. Use it alongside ordinary lighting, visual inspection, monitoring devices and appropriate identification methods. Ultraviolet inspection works because some substances fluoresce when illuminated at a suitable wavelength. The response depends on the material, surface condition, ambient light and the flashlight's actual output. A visible glow is an observation that may warrant further checking; it is not a definitive identification of urine, bed bug evidence, mould, a pesticide residue or another specific substance. Many ordinary materials can fluoresce, and some target residues may not respond clearly. Record what is seen and confirm it using other inspection evidence. The 365nm wavelength is commonly selected for inspection tasks where longer-wave UV-A illumination is useful. It should not be confused with a 395nm decorative blacklight or a germicidal UV-C lamp. These devices have different purposes and safety considerations. The listing does not state optical power, beam angle, battery type, runtime, waterproof rating or included accessories, so those specifications must be checked on the supplied model. Do not infer performance from the wavelength alone. During a property inspection, first make the room safe and use normal white light to understand the surface being examined. Darken the area only as needed to improve visibility, then scan likely inspection points in a controlled pattern. In bed bug work, a UV flashlight may be used as a supplementary aid to inspect selected surfaces, but it does not replace a torch, magnifier, careful examination of seams and joints, or the use of interceptors and other monitoring tools. In hygiene inspections, treat any fluorescent response as a clue rather than a diagnosis. Avoid shining UV light directly into eyes or exposing skin unnecessarily. Do not look into the emitter, reflect the beam toward another person or allow children to play with the flashlight. Use eye protection appropriate to the device and follow the manufacturer's safety instructions. UV-A sources can still present eye and skin exposure risks, particularly with prolonged close-range use. Keep the beam directed at the inspection surface and switch the unit off when not needed. The flashlight can be useful for checking selected hard-to-see areas such as cupboard interiors, corners, under furniture, behind fixtures and around service points. Use a separate mirror or inspection camera where the viewing angle is blocked. If a suspected residue is found, document the location and use an appropriate confirmation method. Do not apply cleaning chemicals or pesticide products simply because a surface fluoresces. Identify the likely material and follow the relevant product or facility procedure. Battery and maintenance details should be confirmed from the exact model supplied. Check the battery compartment, charging port if present, switch operation and lens condition before the first job. Keep the lens clean with a soft cloth and avoid scratching it. Store the flashlight dry and protect it from impact. If rechargeable, use the charging method recommended by the manufacturer and do not leave the unit connected to an unsuitable charger. Replace damaged batteries safely and follow local disposal rules. For Kenyan pest-control contractors, hotels, landlords, cleaning teams and facility managers, a compact UV inspection light can supplement routine surveys in homes, accommodation, offices, warehouses and selected hygiene-sensitive environments. It is a supporting inspection accessory, not a replacement for professional pest…

item.title: Guardmax Zippered Bed Bug Proof Pillow Protectors – 2 Pack
item.description: These Guardmax zippered bed bug pillow protectors are designed to fully enclose pillows and provide a washable physical barrier as part of a bed bug prevention and monitoring routine. The enclosed construction helps reduce accessible hiding places within pillow seams and makes routine inspection and laundering more manageable. This listing is for a two-pack of pillow protectors.
